name: Bob Chew

summary.text: Bob Chew is the Forward Party candidate for U.S. Senate, an engineering consultant and former U.S. Navy officer who has lived in Colorado for almost a decade.
He co-founded an engineering and technical-services company in 1996, sold it to its employees in 2008, and served as its CEO until 2022 and board chair until June 2026.

experience.text: Bachelor's degree, Case Western Reserve University, 1981.
Engineering consultant; co-founded an engineering and technical-services firm in 1996, serving as CEO until 2022 and board chair until June 2026.
Has not previously held elected office.

positions.quote: Tariffs are a tax, plain and simple. They raise prices for consumers, create uncertainty for small businesses, and punish our domestic exporters.
positions.note: He also says he will 'work with any member of Congress to reduce tariffs.'

positions.quote: Different countries and states use different combinations of public and private systems, each with strengths and weaknesses.
positions.note: He explicitly declines to back either expanding government coverage or a market-only approach, instead calling for study of multiple systems' tradeoffs; coded as an explicit middle/mixed position.

positions.quote: Deporting a drug kingpin makes us safer; deporting a local farm hand makes us poorer.
positions.note: He supports removing violent criminals and traffickers but opposes spending resources deporting peaceful, economically-contributing immigrants; coded as an explicit middle/mixed position.

positions.quote: For a decade during the 1990s and early 2000s, Congress restricted assault weapons, and I believe Congress should revisit that approach.
positions.note: He also says he is a gun owner who will defend Second Amendment rights broadly, so this is coded as a qualified rather than unqualified agreement.

positions.quote: I support an all-of-above energy strategy that includes a heavy reliance on nuclear power.
positions.note: He explicitly backs an 'all of the above' mix (including fossil fuels and nuclear) rather than specifically speeding a shift away from oil, gas and coal, and is skeptical wind/solar alone can meet demand; coded as an explicit middle/mixed position.

positions.quote: The United States is one of the only modern democracies where politicians effectively choose their voters through redistricting. That must change.
positions.note: He does not address Colorado's Amendment 86 or mid-decade redistricting specifically; this is inferred from his stated opposition to politician-drawn maps and support for 'eliminating gerrymandering,' which is consistent with favoring independent, commission-drawn maps.

research_notes: Chew completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his campaign website has an unusually detailed issues page for a minor-party candidate, which allowed sourcing more positions than typical for a 'short' profile. No sourced position was found on abortion, guns beyond the assault-weapons point noted, federal public lands, or most 2026 Colorado ballot measures; left unknown rather than inferred. Second pass 2026-10-14: checked the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 Senate candidate Q&A, which Chew did answer; his answers on cost of living, oversight, public lands leasing and immigration reinforce or restate statements already sourced above (deportation-priority) or address topics outside the 25 statements (national debt, oversight generally), so no new position was added.
